solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S060-01.notes: 'Criticized as ___, but drafters chose broad terms deliberately' needs a negative view of broad wording, so 'vague' fits. A 'flexible' is the drafters' positive framing and not a criticism; it is the intended trap. C 'belligerent' (hostile) has no link to broad terms. D 'verbose' means wordy, not imprecise, so it does not fit 'broad terms'.

S060-02.notes: Honeyguides responded far more to the hunters' call than to other human sounds or another bird's calls, so they treat it as a specific signal. A is contradicted by the weaker response to other human sounds. B: honey and wax preference is not tested. C: the study is about responding to calls, not about whether the birds can find nests on their own.

S060-03.notes: The claim is about proportional gain: 90/120 = 75% and 30/80 = 37.5% (about 38%), so C is accurate. A shows only absolute gains (number, not proportion). B compares 2022 levels, not change. D says only that both increased.

S060-04.notes: 'A number of early photographers' is plural, and 'in the decades after 1839' needs the simple past: 'kept their chemical recipes secret'. B 'keeps' is singular and present. C 'has kept' is singular and present perfect, which clashes with the past time frame. D 'was keeping' is singular.

S060-05.notes: The modifier 'Having practiced the search routine...' must be followed directly by the one who practiced, the dog. In A the subject is the volunteer, in B it is the dummy 'it', and in D it is the hiding place, so all three are dangling modifiers. Only C puts 'the dog' right after the comma.

S060-06.notes: After the colon the text gives a positive result (symptoms reduced) and a negative one (the benefit faded), so 'mixed' fits. A 'conclusive' ignores the two-sided outcome. B 'disappointing' leaves out the positive half. C 'unprecedented' is not supported by anything in the text.

S060-07.notes: The text contrasts slow searching of a card catalog in the past with fast online searching now, so 'By contrast' fits. A: the second sentence is not an example of the first. C: the two are opposites, not similar. D: the online catalog does not result from walking between drawers.

S060-08.notes: A is the only choice that states a limitation: with no negative, each image was unique and could not be reproduced. B gives historical facts. C and D describe how the process worked, with no limitation.
